title: Infra GPU Fleet & Cloud Accounts: IaC, CI/CD and Operational Playbook (2026)
author: Ayesha Patel
summary: Operational playbook for managing Redwood's GPU fleet, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC modules, and CI/CD pipelines. Includes capacity targets, ownership matrix, deployment steps, rollback procedures, and runbook excerpts for common operational tasks.
overview: Purpose: provide an opinionated, single-source reference for infra engineers responsible for GPU fleet capacity, cloud account hygiene, networking, IaC modules, and CI/CD build/deploy flows. This playbook consolidates best practices, runbook extracts, and concrete operational procedures used during day-to-day ops and incident responses. Scope: eng-infra (GPU capacity + IaC + CI/CD + cloud accounts + networking). Not in scope: customer-specific private deployment runbooks (see eng-private-deployments).
goals_and_slos:
Primary goals:
- Maintain available GPU capacity to meet Dedicated + Hosted SLOs: 99.95% availability for inference pools, median cold-start latency < 300ms for standard routes.
- Ensure Terraform state and modules are auditable and reproducible across accounts.
- Provide reproducible CI/CD for infra modules with gated promotions and automated canaries.
SLOs and targets:
- GPU pool availability: 99.95% per region per month.
- Provisioning lead time (scale-up): < 15 minutes for warm-up autoscale; < 2 hours for full node provisioning for new capacity.
- IaC pipeline: PR -> plan -> approve -> apply (staged) median time 45m for non-breaking changes.
ownership:
Primary owners:
- GPU Fleet & Capacity: infra/gpu-capacity team (oncall rotation: infra-capacity-rot)
- Terraform modules & IaC: infra-iac team (owner: Marcus Chen)
- Cloud accounts & networking: infra-cloud team (owner: Linnea Berg)
- CI/CD & Pipelines: infra-ci-cd team (owner: Diego Ramos)
Escalation matrix:
1) Pager duty: infra-ops -> infra-sre -> eng-platform -> CTO on critical incidents.
2) For security or RBAC issues escalate to security@redwood; follow incident-response-security playbook.
capacity_planning_and_scaling:
Capacity model overview:
- Pools: Dedicated (reserved), Shared (hosted), Spot-burst (cost-optimized).
- Key metrics to track: GPU utilization (p95/p50), queue length, request QPS by route, average sequence length, KV cache hit rate.
- Buffer policy: target 20% headroom for Hosted pools during business hours; 30% for Black Friday-like events.
Forecasting cadence:
1) Weekly capacity review: review utilization dashboards, new model onboards, and upcoming marketing events.
2) Quarterly capacity audit: update SKU mix, region placement, and cost targets.
Scaling procedures (high-level):
1) Add nodes via IaC: create PR against infra-gpu-pool module with desired node_count/sku.
2) Run terraform plan in staging account and validate plan with infra-ci-cd pipelines.
3) Promote to prod account after canary deploy and smoke tests pass.
4) Verify GPU nodes register with qserv and autoscaling groups.
Validation checklist after scale-up:
- Node count matches desired state.
- Serving runtime versions are consistent.
- Traces show no increased error rates and latency within SLOs.
- Billing alerts updated for capacity change.
cloud_accounts_and_networking:
Account hygiene and networking standards:
- Account structure: org root -> billing -> production accounts (us-west-2, eu-west-1) -> staging -> tooling. Use centralized logging and monitoring accounts for cross-account access.
- VPC per region per account with standardized CIDR blocks (10.<region>.<account>.0/20). Documented in infra-networking repo.
- Peering and Transit: use Transit Gateways (TGW) for cross-account connectivity. Restrict peering to limited use cases; prefer private link endpoints for control-plane services.
- Egress controls: deny-by-default with explicit allowlists for third-party registries and artifact stores.
Firewall and subnet guidance:
- Management subnets for control plane (bastion, jump-hosts) - private with NAT for egress.
- GPU compute subnets - no public IPs. Use private load balancers for internal routing.
- Use security groups with least-privilege and prefix lists for known service IP ranges.
Cross-account access for IaC pipelines:
- CI pipelines assume role into target accounts using short-lived STS creds. Roles are managed centrally (infra-ci-roles).
- Terraform remote state stored in S3/GCS with encryption and ACLs; state locking enabled via DynamoDB or equivalent.
iac_modules_and_patterns:
Module catalog highlights:
- infra-gpu-pool: module used to create node groups, autoscaling configs, and per-pool IAM roles. Inputs: sku, node_count_min/max, patch_window, taints/tolerations.
- infra-networking: VPC, subnets, TGW attachments, route tables, endpoint configurations.
- infra-iam: standardized roles for services (ci-runner, kube-controller, autoscaler).
IiC patterns and best practices:
- Keep modules small and composable. Each module must have input validation, examples, and acceptance tests.
- Module lifecycle: develop -> unit tests -> integration canary in staging -> documentation -> semver bump -> promote.
- State migration rules: document manual migration steps in module release notes when changing resource addresses or moving to new locking primitives.
Terraform pipeline behavior:
- PR triggers terraform fmt, validate, and unit tests.
- Merging to main triggers a staged plan in staging account. After automated checks pass an approver (module owner) manually approves promotion to prod.
- All plans are stored as artifacts and linked from PRs for audit.
ci_cd_and_build_pipelines:
Pipeline layout:
- repos: infra-iac, infra-gpu, infra-networking, infra-ci-templates.
- Pipelines: PR -> lint/format -> unit tests -> terratest/integration -> plan -> gated-approve -> apply -> smoke-tests.
- Canary strategy: apply to a single region/account subset first, run workload smoke tests for 30m, then roll out to remaining accounts.
Security and gating:
- Mandatory code owners on critical modules.
- Automated checks: static-analysis (tfsec), policy-as-code (opa), IAM diff checks.
- Secrets: use HashiCorp Vault or cloud KMS; no secrets in repo.
Observability for pipelines:
- Each run emits structured logs and metrics to the infra-monitoring account. Build failures automatically notify owners via Slack and create a ticket in the infra backlog board.
runbooks_and_incident_playbook:
Quick runbooks (excerpts):
A) GPU pool degraded (high error rate / OOMs):
1) Verify alerts: query "gpu-pool-error-rate" and "oom-count" dashboards.
2) Check recent deploys: git log on infra-gpu and runtime release notes.
3) If CPU/driver crash suspected: cordon affected nodes, collect dmesg + journald, and escalate to runtime team.
4) Fallback: shift traffic to compatible model variant or warm spare pool following routing guide.
5) Post-incident: run regression triage and update quantization/profile configs if needed.
B) Terraform apply failed in prod: partial apply with drift:
1) Immediately pause dependent pipelines and flag manual-change incident.
2) Check Terraform state for locks and apply attempt artifacts.
3) Re-run plan with -refresh=false to see resources that changed outside IaC.
4) If recovery requires re-apply: create emergency PR, link incident, and require 2 approvers before apply.
C) New capacity emergency (unexpected traffic spike):
1) Bypass usual staging canary: change pool desired_count via emergency API flag (requires infra-capacity lead).
2) Monitor queue lengths and latency; if scaling fails, convert low-priority routes to degraded mode.
3) After stabilization: backfill IaC change and follow postmortem flow.
Post-incident steps:
- Ownership: incident owner writes postmortem within 72 hours.
- Metrics: include p95/p99 latency, error budget impact, capacity utilization charts.
- Action items: assign to owners with target dates and track in quarterly reliability initiatives.
deployment_checklist_and_templates:
Pre-deploy checklist (short):
- PR has plan artifact and no tfsec/opa failures.
- Integration tests passed in staging.
- Owners and approvers assigned.
- Monitoring dashboards updated for new resources.
- Billing alarms updated for capacity delta.
Deployment template (example commit message):
- Title: "infra(gpu-pool): scale us-west-2 standard-pool +8 nodes (sku A100)"
- Body: reason, link to plan artifact, smoke test commands, rollback plan, owner, ETA.
Rollback criteria and actions:
- Rollback trigger: error rate > 2% above baseline for 15m or latency p95 increase > 30% for 10m.
- Action: revert IaC change, apply revert in staging and then prod, and re-evaluate.
